states.changed: A reader points at any of the 80 report days in a funnel, sees that day zone by zone, and sees on a strip of the table's column labels that both outlying days carry the same wording as their neighbours.

A fourth figure sets Ituri's 51 report days from 30 August to 1 November in order, shades the days whose line on the dead writes failures, and shows beside them the two pooled shares (33.1 % and 28.3 %) with their intervals; a reader can read each day's line and count, and move the share to the next report day.

A fifth figure lays reports 108 to 174 side by side in three rows (the program version that made each PDF, Ituri's sentence on the dead, North Kivu's) with the six missing reports hatched, so a reader sees the make and both sentences change together across the hole in which North Kivu stops writing “sans échec”, and can read each report's make and sentences.

A sixth figure sets the 80 report days side by side with every zone row the parser threw away, coloured by why, and a reader can point at 6 or 30 October to see that no zone was missing: one wrapped cell and seven readable rows, six of whose rates were carried over from the day before; Figure 4 now carries a dated correction.

A seventh figure sets 62 pairs of consecutive report days side by side with every zone whose running total of deaths did not move by the deaths it printed that day, and a reader can point at 30 October to see that Ituri's total carried the province row's 19 deaths, not its zones' 21.
